junior.title: Shows loading and error states
good_looks_like: Every screen that loads data shows a loading state, an error state with a way to retry, and an empty state.
explain_angles: What does the user see while this loads?
What does the user see if it fails?

drills.prompt: A list page fetches orders. Describe every state the page can be in and what the user sees in each.

key_points.text: Loading: a spinner or skeleton
Error: a message and a retry action
Empty: a clear 'no orders yet' state
Success: the list

drills.prompt: Users say a page 'goes blank' on slow networks. What is probably missing, and how do you fix it?

key_points.text: No loading state while data is on its way
Possibly no error state when the request fails
Add explicit states and test with a slow network in dev tools

red_flags.text: Blames the network and changes nothing

react.note: Model loading, error and data as explicit state, or use a data library that gives isLoading and error.

nextjs.note: Add loading.js and error.js next to the route for loading and error states.

angular.note: Track loading and error in the component or a signal, and show them in the template.

junior.why_it_matters: Without loading and error states, users see a blank or frozen screen and think the app is broken.

junior.title: Never swallows a failed request
good_looks_like: A failed request is shown to the user or handled on purpose; it is never only logged to the console.
explain_angles: What does the user see when this request fails?
Why is a console message not enough here?

drills.prompt: A save button calls the API with .catch(console.error). What does the user experience when the save fails, and what would you do?

key_points.text: The user thinks it saved; their change is silently lost
Show an error and keep their input so they can retry
Report the error to monitoring, not only the console

drills.prompt: When is it fine to ignore a failed request in the UI? Give an example.

key_points.text: When the data is optional and the page works without it
A concrete example such as a non-critical recommendation widget
Still report it so the team knows it fails

react.note: Put the error in state and render it; do not end a promise chain with console.error.

nextjs.note: Let errors reach an error.js boundary or show them in the form state.

angular.note: Handle errors in the subscribe error callback or catchError and show them to the user.

junior.why_it_matters: A failed request that is only logged loses the user's work silently and leaves them confused.

mid.title: Checks the response before using it
good_looks_like: Checks the HTTP status before reading the body, and turns a failed status into a real error.
explain_angles: What happens here if the server answers 500?
Why check the status before reading the body?

drills.prompt: fetch() resolved, so the code calls res.json() and renders it. The server answered 500 with an HTML page. What happens, and how should the code be written?

key_points.text: fetch only rejects on network errors, not on 4xx or 5xx
res.json() fails on HTML or the app renders an error body as data
Check res.ok or the status first and throw a real error

red_flags.text: Believes fetch rejects on HTTP errors

drills.prompt: Where would you put response checking so every screen gets it, and what would it return?

key_points.text: In one shared API client or wrapper
It throws a typed error with status and message
Screens then handle one error shape

red_flags.text: Copies the check into every component

react.note: Wrap fetch in one client function that checks res.ok and throws a typed error.

nextjs.note: Check res.ok in server fetches too, and call notFound() or throw for error.js.

angular.note: HttpClient errors on non-2xx; use an interceptor to map them to one error type.

mid.why_it_matters: fetch does not fail on a server error; reading an error page as data breaks the screen in strange ways.

mid.title: Cancels stale requests
good_looks_like: When the user moves on or types again, old requests are cancelled or ignored so a slow old answer never overwrites a new one.
explain_angles: What happens if the user types fast here?
What happens if they leave the page before it loads?

drills.prompt: A search box fetches results on each key press. Sometimes old results appear after new ones. Why, and how do you fix it?

key_points.text: Responses can arrive out of order: a race
Cancel the previous request (AbortController, switchMap) or ignore stale answers
Debounce the input to send fewer requests

red_flags.text: Says requests always come back in order

drills.prompt: A component starts a fetch and the user navigates away before it finishes. What can go wrong, and what do you do?

key_points.text: State updates on a gone component, or wasted work
Abort in the effect cleanup or unsubscribe on destroy
Ignore AbortError so it is not shown as a failure

red_flags.text: Shows the abort as an error to the user

react.note: Create an AbortController in the effect and abort it in the cleanup function.

nextjs.note: On the client, the same effect cleanup applies; prefer a data library that cancels for you.

angular.note: Use switchMap so a new search cancels the old request.

mid.why_it_matters: Old answers arriving late overwrite new ones and show the wrong data, a bug that is hard to reproduce.

mid.title: Caches and dedupes server data on purpose
good_looks_like: Chooses how long data can be stale, avoids fetching the same data twice, and refreshes it after a change.
explain_angles: How fresh must this data be?

drills.prompt: Three components on one page each fetch the current user. What problems does that cause, and how do you fix it?

key_points.text: Three requests for the same data: waste and possible mismatch
Share one cached query or lift the fetch up
Decide when the cached user is refreshed

red_flags.text: Caches forever with no way to refresh

drills.prompt: After a user edits their profile, the header still shows the old name. Why, and what is the right fix?

key_points.text: A cache holds the old data
Invalidate or update the cached data after the change
Optionally update it right away and roll back on failure

react.note: Use a server-state library (for example TanStack Query) with query keys and invalidation.

nextjs.note: Know the fetch cache and revalidate after a change with revalidatePath or revalidateTag.

angular.note: Share one observable with shareReplay or a store, and refresh it after writes.

mid.why_it_matters: Fetching the same data again and again wastes time, and stale data after a change confuses users.

senior.title: Designs for slow and flaky networks
good_looks_like: The app stays usable on slow or dropping connections: safe retries, optimistic updates with rollback, and clear offline states.
explain_angles: What does this screen do on a train with a weak signal?
What happens to the user's change if the request fails?

drills.prompt: Users on mobile complain that 'liking' a post feels slow and sometimes gets lost. How would you redesign it?

key_points.text: Optimistic update: show the like at once
Roll back and tell the user if the request finally fails
Retry safely; the server action must be idempotent

red_flags.text: Shows success with no rollback when it fails

drills.prompt: Which requests should the frontend retry automatically, and which never? Why?

key_points.text: Retry safe reads and idempotent writes
Never auto-retry non-idempotent writes like a payment without a key
Use backoff and a cap

react.note: Use optimistic updates with rollback (useOptimistic or your data library's onMutate).

nextjs.note: Combine server actions with useOptimistic and show pending state.

angular.note: Use rxjs retry with a delay for safe calls, and update state optimistically with rollback.

senior.why_it_matters: Real users are on slow and flaky networks; an app that only works on fast Wi-Fi loses their actions and their trust.

senior.title: Recovers from errors with boundaries
good_looks_like: A crash in one part of the screen is caught and replaced with a fallback, so the rest of the app keeps working, and the error is reported.
explain_angles: Why put the boundary here and not higher?
What does the user see when this part breaks?

drills.prompt: A bug in a sidebar widget makes the whole dashboard go white. How do you stop one widget from taking down the page?

key_points.text: Wrap the widget in its own error boundary
Show a small fallback with a retry
Report the error to monitoring

red_flags.text: One boundary around the whole app only

drills.prompt: Which errors does an error boundary NOT catch, and how do you handle those?

key_points.text: Errors in event handlers and async code
Handle them in the handler or put them in state so they render
Global handlers for unhandled rejections, for reporting

red_flags.text: Says a boundary catches every error

react.note: Place error boundaries around independent parts of the screen.

nextjs.note: Add error.js at route segments so one segment fails alone.

angular.note: Provide a custom ErrorHandler for reporting and show fallbacks per component.

senior.why_it_matters: One broken widget should not blank the whole page; boundaries keep the rest of the app usable.

staff.title: Sets the data-fetching standard for an app
good_looks_like: Chooses one data-fetching approach, one API client and one error shape for the whole app, and makes them easy to use right.
explain_angles: Why should every screen fetch data this way?
How do new screens get this right by default?

drills.prompt: Your app mixes three ways of fetching data and bugs keep coming from stale data and missing errors. What standard would you set and how would you move the app to it?

key_points.text: Pick one server-state approach and one API client
One error shape and shared loading and error components
Migrate screen by screen, with lint rules or review checks
Measure it, for example with error reports or bug counts

drills.prompt: How would you decide what data is fetched on the server and what on the client?

key_points.text: Server for first paint, SEO and secrets
Client for user-specific, fast-changing or interactive data
Consider caching and how fresh each kind must be

red_flags.text: Everything on the client by habit

react.note: Standardise on one server-state library and a typed API client.

nextjs.note: Decide server vs client fetching per route and document caching rules.

angular.note: Use one HttpClient wrapper with interceptors and one state approach.

staff.why_it_matters: Three ways of fetching data in one app means three kinds of bugs; one standard makes every new screen right by default.
